newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end marginally lower ahead of supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end marginally lower ahead of supply.

text.p: Prices of U.S. Treasury securities ended lower but little changed from Friday's closing levels on Monday in a low-volume, data-sparse trading session.
Without any fresh economic releases to provide direction, the market focused on upcoming supply, which weighed on prices as the day unfolded.
The U.S. Treasury is scheduled to auction $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.
"By default the two- and five-year auctions have become the market's main focus for the next couple of days," said Anthony Karydakis, senior financial economist at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc.
"Given the fact that you have a clear economic calendar for most of the week, and due to the upcoming supply, it's only understandable for the market to go through a consolidation phase," he added.
The benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond was down 3/32 at 99-9/32 to yield 6.81 percent in late Monday trade. The 6.0 percent two-year note was down 1/32 at 100-6/32 to yield 5.89 percent.

Prices began the day in positive territory after strength in foreign bond markets and overseas dollar gains spurred buying interest. However, as the session unfolded, dealers began positioning themselves for the auctions and early gains were erased.
Despite Monday's modest price retreat, market observers said the mood remains positive.
"The mood is positive but tentative," said Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities Inc. "We just don't have much new on the data front until Friday and next week looms even larger."
On Friday, the market will digest the September durable goods report. Next week, reports on third quarter Gross Domestic Product growth and October employment will highlight a busy calendar.
Separately, the Treasury sold $26.0 billion in three- and six-month bills at its regular weekly auction on Monday at average rates of 5.01 percent and 5.12 percent, respectively.

In late trade, three-month bill rates were up one basis point at 4.99 percent, six-month bill rates were up three basis points at 5.12 percent and year-bill rates had risen one basis point to 5.24 percent. CORPORATE BONDS
Corporate bond spreads were firm in typically light Monday trade, except for deep losses in debt from TCI Communications Inc and MobileMedia Corp, dealers said.

MobileMedia's 9-3/8 percent debt traded off more than 10 basis points from Friday's close, traders said, following the company's announcement that it may default on about $11 million in November debt service.
The company first said third quarter earnings could place it in violation of certain bank covenants in late September.
Elsewhere, traders pushed TCI debt 15 basis points wider following a negative outlook by Standard & Poor's credit rating agency late on Friday.
In light new issuance, BankAmerica Corp issued $250 million A2/single-A rated subordinated notes due 2011 as 7.125s to yield 7.218 percent or 72 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Also, May Department Stores set $125 million 20-year A2/single-A rated debentures at par to yield 7.45 percent or 64 basis points over the Treasury long bond. MUNICIPAL BONDS
Municipal bond prices fell from one-eighth to one-quarter of a point in late afternoon trade on Monday as traders fretted about an unusually large amount of new issues scheduled for sale this week.
As much as $4.8 billion of new offerings are expected to be sold this week, with nearly half of this sum set for Tuesday, when almost $2.2 million of new debt will come to market.

"We have a pretty large new issue calender. The feeling is you may see some selling to make room," a trader said. However, he added that potential buyers appeared to be holding off until they see if the new debt is attractively priced.
